rawCommits.subject: fix(observability): clean up status probe agents (#69)
feat(analytics): capture first-touch acquisition source
rawCommits.body:
Classify each visitor's first-touch referrer + utm_source into a clean
acquisition_source label (x, google, direct, or the site's own domain for
anything else) and stamp it once via register_once, so it survives return
visits and rides on every client event. Mirror it onto the user profile
with people.set_once at identify time so server-emitted events like
session_active (True DAU) can also be broken down by source. Lets us see
where signups and engaged/retained users actually come from instead of
guessing. Adds classifier + pipeline tests.

rawCommits.subject: fix(analytics): report a single app_version for the web surface
rawCommits.body:
The Render web build stamps APP_VERSION=$RENDER_GIT_COMMIT, so every deploy
baked a fresh commit SHA into app_version and Mixpanel showed a new web
version per deploy. Web is a single continuously-deployed surface, so
getAppVersion() now reports the unversioned 0.0.0 label for the web platform
(one line in analytics) while desktop and mobile keep their real baked
release versions. The exact web build stays recoverable via
getBuildInfo().commit (bug reports). Affects only the analytics app_version
super-property and the X-App-Version header; no build or validator change.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: report a single app_version for the web surface

rawCommits.subject: fix(skills): write the required name field into skill frontmatter
rawCommits.body:
User-created skills were written with a SKILL.md frontmatter that omitted
the name field. The harness parser requires it (SkillFrontmatter.name), so
a name-less file fails to load and the skill is dropped from the in-memory
registry on every reload — a skill worked right after creation (the
registry still held the harness's own name-bearing copy) but vanished with
"skill not found" after the next harness restart, which is why editing
broke for existing skills after the last deploy.

render_skill_frontmatter now writes name (used by both create and edit), so
the marker file the harness reloads from is always loadable. Reproduced
against the real harness: the name-less shape is rejected, the fixed shape
loads. Tests assert the field is present on create and edit.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: write the required name field into skill frontmatter

rawCommits.subject: fix(skills): recover skills orphaned by the missing-name bug on startup
rawCommits.body:
Skills created before the name: frontmatter fix have a SKILL.md the harness
cannot load (no name: field), so they were dropped from the registry and
show "skill not found". A startup repair pass backfills name: (derived from
the skill's directory) into any user-created skill missing it, so the harness
loads them again on its next reload. Marker-gated (only touches files
carrying source: "user-created" — never shop skills), idempotent, and
fail-soft; writes atomically (temp + rename) so a concurrent harness reload
cannot read a half-written file.

Verified end to end against the real harness: an orphaned skill returns 404
before repair and loads (200) after. Unit tests cover backfill / idempotency
/ name-bearing-untouched / no-marker-untouched / invalid-name-skipped; an
integration test exercises the real startup entry point.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: recover skills orphaned by the missing-name bug on startup

rawCommits.subject: fix(skills): reset the edit modal's fields on open
rawCommits.body:
The skill editor reused its form state across opens, so a slow or failed
getSkill left the previously-edited skill's description/instructions in the
form — which looked like it "pulled up the last skill." Reset the fields at
the start of the load effect so the form only ever shows the skill actually
being edited (empty + error on a failed load, never stale content). Adds a
test that switching to a skill whose load fails clears the prior content.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: reset the edit modal's fields on open

rawCommits.subject: fix(skills): pre-fill the edit form from the marker file, not the harness
rawCommits.body:
Editing pre-filled the form from getSkill (a verbatim harness proxy), but the
harness response drops user_invocable / model_invocable / allowed_tools
(field-name mismatches + no model_invocable concept), so saving an edit
silently reset those — a regression unmasked once the name: fix made editing
actually run.

Add GET /api/harness/skills/mine/{name} (get_my_skill) that reads the
user-created marker file (the source of truth) and returns every field
faithfully, with the same 400/404/403 guards as update_my_skill. The edit
modal now pre-fills from it. Verified: create with user_invocable=false /
model_invocable=true / allowed_tools, and get_my_skill returns them intact
(getSkill would have lost all three). Tests: round-trip + 404 + 403 backend,
modal pre-fill frontend.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: pre-fill the edit form from the marker file, not the harness

rawCommits.subject: fix(skills): run skill recovery on the desktop startup path too
rawCommits.body:
The desktop embeds aura-os-server as a library (it calls build_app_state
directly), so aura-os-server's own main() — where repair_user_skills_on_startup
was wired — never runs on desktop. That left the recovery dead for desktop
users, who are exactly the ones hitting orphaned skills. Call it from the
desktop's own main() (mirroring the adjacent ensure_user_bins_on_path), before
the server and harness start, so orphaned skills are repaired before the
harness loads them.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: run skill recovery on the desktop startup path too

rawCommits.subject: test(skills): verify the full edit cycle preserves every setting
rawCommits.body:
End-to-end proof for the round-trip fix: create a skill with non-default
flags + allowed_tools/model/context, open it for edit (get_my_skill), save
changing only the description, and re-open — every other setting survives.
Guards against a regression where editing silently reset user_invocable /
model_invocable / allowed_tools.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: verify the full edit cycle preserves every setting

rendered.title: Skills recovery, manual tasks, and cleaner analytics
rendered.intro: Today's nightly is anchored by a thorough rescue of user-created skills — a missing frontmatter field had been quietly orphaning them across reloads — alongside a real fix for adding tasks without a spec, sharper acquisition analytics, and a swarm cleanup that stops abandoned probe agents from piling up.

entries.title: Swarm status probes get a real teardown path
entries.summary: Deleting a swarm-backed agent now drives the remote gateway through stop-then-delete, so observability probes stop accumulating as ghost agents.

items.text: Agent deletion now detects swarm-mode agents and calls the swarm gateway's delete endpoint, retrying through a stop step when the gateway returns 409, so remote probe agents are reliably removed instead of being left running.
The status-probe runner and its new tests round out the cleanup, giving the eval pipeline a way to verify probes are torn down end to end.

entries.title: First-touch acquisition source in analytics
entries.summary: The web analytics pipeline now tells us where users actually came from, and stops inventing a brand new app version on every deploy.

items.text: Each visitor's first-touch referrer and utm_source are classified into a tidy acquisition_source label (x, google, direct, the site's own domain, etc.), stamped once via register_once, and mirrored onto the user profile at identify time so server-side events like session_active can be broken down by source.

Web now reports a single stable app_version (0.0.0) to Mixpanel instead of a fresh commit SHA per Render deploy, while desktop and mobile keep their real baked release versions; the exact web build is still recoverable from getBuildInfo().commit.

entries.title: Rescuing user-created skills from the missing-name bug
entries.summary: A four-part fix restores skills that had been silently dropped from the harness registry and stops the skill editor from quietly resetting fields on save.

items.text: Created and edited skills now write the required name: field into SKILL.md frontmatter, so the harness can load them on every reload instead of dropping them with "skill not found" after a restart.

A startup repair pass backfills name: into any user-created skill missing it, marker-gated to user-authored files and written atomically so a concurrent harness reload can't read a half-written file — orphaned skills now load on the next reload.

The skill editor now pre-fills from a new GET /api/harness/skills/mine/{name} endpoint that reads the marker file directly, so user_invocable, model_invocable, and allowed_tools round-trip faithfully instead of being silently reset on save.
The edit modal also clears its form at the start of every load, so a slow or failed fetch can no longer leave the previously-edited skill's description and instructions sitting in the form.

entries.title: Skill recovery extended to the desktop startup path
entries.summary: Desktop users — the ones most affected by orphaned skills — now actually run the new recovery pass.

items.text: Because desktop embeds aura-os-server as a library and never executes its main(), repair_user_skills_on_startup is now invoked explicitly from the desktop's own startup before the server and harness boot, so orphaned skills are repaired before the harness tries to load them.

entries.title: End-to-end guard for the skill edit round-trip
entries.summary: A new integration test locks in the editor fix so flags and tool lists can't silently regress again.

items.text: An end-to-end test creates a skill with non-default user_invocable, model_invocable, allowed_tools, model, and context, edits only its description, and re-opens it to confirm every other setting survives — closing the regression where editing silently reset those fields.

entries.title: Manual tasks, literal chat prompts, and steadier browser defaults
entries.summary: A QA-blocker sweep across chat, browser, and the Tasks board unblocks adding ad-hoc tasks and stops a few small but visible misbehaviors.

items.text: Tasks can now be created without a spec: the server auto-resolves (or creates) a "Manual Tasks" spec when none is supplied, broadcasts the new spec, and a follow-up fix gives manual tasks a sensible default order_index so they slot into the board correctly.
Chat now preserves literal prompt text in the input bar instead of transforming it, fixing cases where typed prompts were subtly altered before send.
The browser session resolver no longer falls back to stale probe URLs as defaults, so new sessions start from a clean state.

highlights: User-created skills no longer vanish after a reload
Manual tasks can be added without picking a spec
First-touch acquisition source captured in analytics
Swarm status probes now actually get torn down
